adjudication.reason: The route's local `resolveUser` helper collapses FOUR different conditions into one `null`: no database client, no access-token cookie, an invalid token, and no ACTIVE organization membership. The handler then answers **HTTP 401 "Authentication required"**. So during a database outage an already-authenticated academy user is told their authentication is required. No data is served, which is the right direction — but the status is wrong in a way that matters twice over: the user is sent to re-authenticate pointlessly, and every authentication-failure monitor in the platform fills with infrastructure noise that is indistinguishable from a real credential problem.

adjudication.reason: `isAccountLocked` returns **`false`** — "not locked" — when there is no database. The account-lockout control therefore does not apply during an outage. It is NOT exploitable on its own: the password check is Prisma-backed too, and `issueTokens` throws `SessionPersistenceError` in database mode, so the handler answers 503 and no login can succeed. The defect is that the control's SAFE answer is its ABSENT answer: were the lockout ever consulted on a path that does not also need the database, the fail-open would be live. Together with DB-06 (the counter is never incremented and `login.failed` is never emitted) the entire brute-force defence is inert during an outage.

adjudication.reason: The handler builds the site-isolation filter inside a POSITIVE guard with no else: `if (allowedSiteIds.length > 0) { const db = await getPrisma(); if (db) { … allowedAssetIds = new Set(...) } }`. When Prisma is absent, `allowedAssetIds` stays `undefined` — and `getKnowledgeGraph` documents `undefined` as "OWNER/ADMIN full-access", i.e. NO site filter. The site-scope restriction therefore degrades to full access on a database outage. It is NOT currently exploitable: `loadOrgGraph` calls `getPrisma()` as well and returns `null` on the same condition, so the graph is empty and the unfiltered path has nothing to disclose; the endpoint answers HTTP 200 with zero nodes and writes a GRAPH_QUERY audit row recording nodeCount 0. The defect is LATENT and structural — any cache, snapshot or in-process fallback added to the graph loader (the pattern DB-F1 already uses elsewhere in this repository) would make the bypass live for site-restricted actors within their organisation. Cross-tenant exposure is not possible: `loadOrgGraph` filters on `organizationId` unconditionally.
